name: Containers
blurb: Every separately deployable or storable part of the runtime request path, and the traffic between them. Build, deploy and alerting machinery lives on the Delivery tab. C4 level 2.
audience: Platform engineers, and anyone reviewing a change
note: Web ACLs, Shield and the VPC are not containers — they are policy and network attached to the boxes below, so each one's effect is a fact on the container it guards and an entry in that container's resource list. Note what is absent: FLEX owns no datastore, no queue and no event bus, so every user request is a synchronous fan-out that has to finish inside a 20 to 30 second Lambda timeout.

d.role: Everything CloudFront insists on owning: the distribution, its two functions, the CLOUDFRONT-scope Web ACL, the certificate and the spec bucket.
facts: The alarm actions in this region publish to us-east-1 relay topics, because a CloudWatch alarm cannot target a topic in another region. The relay itself is on the Delivery tab.

d.role: Where an origin request first meets FLEX-owned compute, and the only place a user's token is actually verified.

d.tech: eu-west-2 · one CloudFormation stack per domain
d.role: Business logic. One stack per domain, one Lambda per route, no shared runtime between them.
facts: A domain team writes a domain.config.ts and handler files; the stack, the routes, the IAM and the alarms are generated from that config.

Domains are coupled at build time as well as at runtime: dvla, groups, uns and example all take a workspace dependency on @flex/udp-domain, and three of them import a udp Zod response schema straight into their own domain.config.ts — a udp schema change breaks them at compile time.

d.tech: API Gateway PRIVATE + three gateway Lambdas
d.role: The only route from a domain to an upstream: a private API in front of the three functions that hold the credentials.
facts: No domain function holds an upstream credential; the credential lives in the gateway function and the domain is only allowed to invoke the route ARNs its own config names.

d.role: Every system FLEX brokers. All user state lives here.
facts: FLEX owns no datastore: there is no database, queue or event bus in the repo — the only data store on this diagram is the spec bucket.

d.role: Calls the public API through CloudFront.
facts: The only real-user caller of the request path below; the smoke-test canary is the other production caller.

d.role: The single public entry point for the API. (Development also exposes an unauthenticated JWKS stub Function URL.)
facts: Default behaviour: the API origin with caching disabled and ALL_VIEWER_EXCEPT_HOST_HEADER, plus the x-origin-verify header the origin demands.
/docs* behaviour: the spec bucket through Origin Access Control, caching optimised — the only cached behaviour on the distribution.

Guarded by a CLOUDFRONT-scope Web ACL — two managed rule groups, IP reputation, a 2000-per-IP rate limit and an end-to-end test bypass header — and by Shield Advanced, which is only created outside development.

d.role: Correlation ID and structural JWT validation at the edge.
facts: Rejects a missing or structurally invalid token with a 401 before the origin is touched; the signature is checked for presence only, never verified.

Sets x-correlation-id on every request to the API behaviour, so every Lambda log line carries it. The /docs* behaviour runs a different function that does not; API Gateway access logs do not include it.

d.role: Rewrites /docs and /docs/ to the Swagger UI index.
facts: /docs redirects 301 to /docs/, which rewrites to /docs/index.html. It touches no headers.

d.role: Swagger UI plus one generated OpenAPI 3.1 document per domain.
facts: Deployed with prune:false, so specs for domains no longer generated are not deleted. The generator always emits all domains' specs regardless of the deploy target.
Private: BlockPublicAccess.BLOCK_ALL, reachable only through the distribution's Origin Access Control.

d.role: Hosts /health and the /app tree every domain attaches to.
facts: Origin-locked by a REGIONAL Web ACL whose default action is block — only a request carrying the x-origin-verify secret is allowed through, which is what makes the raw execute-api URL unusable.
Custom 401 and 403 gateway responses surface the authorizer's errorMessage to the caller.

d.role: TOKEN authorizer verifying the Cognito access token.
facts: Returns a policy carrying pairwiseId in the authorizer context; on an allow the policy resource is *, not the invoked method ARN.
Emits one of six auth telemetry events on every decision. An expired token is the only denial that carries a message.

d.role: Issues and signs the access tokens FLEX accepts.
facts: A sibling GOV.UK Once system, not a third party. In development the authorizer is pointed at a stub user pool and at FLEX's own JWKS Function URL instead.

d.type: Container group · one Lambda per route
d.role: Driving licence, vehicles, share codes, vehicle enquiry.
facts: The only domain whose common.access is private, so its route functions sit in the egress tier and can reach NAT.

Depends on udp: six of its eight routes fetch the DVLA linking ID from udp's private identity route in parallel with a DVLA authenticate call (vehicle-enquiry needs only the token). Its other nine integrations all target the DVLA gateway.
development, staging and production, plus every ephemeral PR and personal stage.

d.type: Container group · one Lambda per route
d.role: Identity links, user upsert, notification preferences.
facts: The hub of the domain graph: dvla, uns, groups and example all call its private routes — GET /v1/users/push-id for three of them, GET /v1/identity/{service} for dvla.
Depends outward on the DVLA gateway for the well-known JWKS, and on the dvla domain's private unlink route — but only when the environment parameter reads production.
development, staging and production, plus every ephemeral PR and personal stage.

d.type: Container group · one Lambda per route
d.role: Notification listing, read status and deletion.
facts: Depends on udp only: all four routes fetch the push ID from udp's private route, then call the UNS gateway with it.
development, staging and production, plus every ephemeral PR and personal stage.

d.type: Container group · one Lambda per route
d.role: Group subscription read and update.
facts: An uncompensated dual write: POST /v1/groups writes the UNS gateway, merges the result with the user's current UDP groups, then writes the UDP gateway. A UDP failure after a UNS success throws BadGateway and leaves the two systems of record divergent — no compensation, no idempotency key. It is the one place FLEX orchestrates a multi-system transaction.
Depends on udp (the private push-ID route plus two udp gateway routes) and on the uns gateway.
development and staging, plus every ephemeral PR and personal stage.

d.type: Container group · one Lambda per route
d.role: Reference domain demonstrating every SDK capability.
facts: Exercises feature flags, all four resource types and both integration kinds, including one that calls its own private POST /v0/todos.
Depends on udp (the private push-ID route and two udp gateway routes) and on the uns gateway.
development, plus every ephemeral PR and personal stage — the environments list is only enforced for persistent stages.

d.type: Container group · one Lambda per route
d.role: Local authority read and upsert.
facts: Private-only, so its stack creates no authorizer and nothing reaches it from the public API — which is why it has no line from pubapi.

Broken today: both of its integrations name /v1/local-council routes on the udp gateway, which defines no such routes, so the gateway's own lookup returns 404. pnpm validate:integrations does not catch it — it only checks type: domain integrations.
development and staging, plus every ephemeral PR and personal stage.

d.role: The internal routing plane: /health, /domains/** and /gateways/**.
facts: Only reachable through the API Gateway interface endpoint — the resource policy denies every other source and adds no Allow, so the caller's own IAM policy is the sole gate.
AuthorizationType.IAM on every method, so every caller must SigV4-sign.
dataTraceEnabled is false, keeping internal request and response bodies out of the logs.

d.role: Sole holder of DVLA credentials.
facts: Mounted at ANY /gateways/dvla/{proxy+}: its ten routes are matched inside the handler, not by API Gateway, so an unknown path returns the gateway's own 404.
In the egress tier because DVLA is reached over the internet through NAT.
Mints a fresh X-Correlation-Id per client build rather than propagating one — the chain has already ended at the private-API turn (see Request path).

d.role: Sole holder of UDP credentials.
facts: SigV4 with credentials from sts:AssumeRole, optionally carrying an ExternalId, plus an x-api-key header set per route.

No internet route — isolated subnets, no NAT. The UDP endpoint it dials comes from consumerConfig.apiUrl (not in this repo); reachability depends on that URL resolving through the API Gateway interface endpoint. Unlike UNS, the udp consumer-config schema has no privateApiUrl field at all.

d.role: Sole holder of UNS credentials.
facts: Dials consumerConfig.privateApiUrl with a SigV4-signed assumed role, with X-API-KEY set once on the client for every route.

d.role: Licence, vehicle and share-code services.
facts: The only upstream outside the GOV.UK Once boundary, and the only one reached over the public internet.

d.role: Identity and preference store.
facts: The gateway dials consumerConfig.apiUrl, and the udp consumer-config schema has no privateApiUrl field, so whether this hop stays inside AWS depends on what that URL resolves to.

d.role: Notification and group store.
facts: Its consumer config names a privateApiUrl, and that is the URL the UNS gateway dials.

d.role: Countries and events for the travel feature.
facts: environments is development and staging only, so it does not exist in production.
Both routes are public on /app/travel/** and reach the travel gateway over the private API.

d.role: Sole holder of the travel upstream credentials.
facts: Runs in the egress tier because it reaches DynamoDB and STS over the public AWS endpoints through NAT, which isolated subnets cannot route to.
environments is development and staging only.

d.role: The shared sources table and the event store.
facts: Reached by assuming roleArn from the consumer-config secret — not an HTTP API like the other three upstreams.
The sources table holds every namespace, not only travel.
The distribution's Web ACL and its viewer-request function both sit on this hop; the repo does not pin down which runs first, so neither does this diagram.
Associated with the default behaviour only — a /docs* request runs the docs function instead.
The only cached behaviour on the distribution.
The secret is generated in eu-west-2 and replicated to us-east-1.
Without this header the regional Web ACL's default block applies.

d.carries: The Authorization header out; an IAM policy and pairwiseId back
facts: resultsCacheTtl is never set, so API Gateway's five-minute default cache applies — and because the allow policy's resource is *, one cached allow covers every route.
Each domain stack with public routes creates its own TokenAuthorizer over this one shared function.
There is no cognito-idp interface endpoint, so this call leaves the VPC through the NAT gateway. In development it points at the stub Function URL instead.
Development, plus every ephemeral PR and personal stage.

d.auth: SigV4 with the route function's own role
d.carries: Nine DVLA gateway calls plus the udp linking-ID domain call
facts: Each route function gets an inline policy naming only the route ARNs listed in that route's integrations array.

UNS gateway calls plus the UDP push-ID domain call
UNS and UDP gateway calls plus the UDP push-ID domain call
Two udp gateway calls out; two private routes in

facts: Includes a self-integration: example calls its own private POST /v0/todos.

facts: Declared and deployed, but no domain integrates with them.
One ANY {proxy+} method per gateway; the gateway function matches the path itself.

facts: The only egress out of the VPC to a non-AWS destination. (The canary also reaches One Login and Firebase, but it runs outside the VPC.)

tables.name: The three Lambda access tiers
rows: On, and there is no prop to turn them off
tables.note: All three share the rest: NODEJS_24_X, Tracing.ACTIVE, a 10-second default timeout, a log group at one year, environmentEncryption from resolveEncryptionKey() with grantDecrypt to the function, FLEX_ENVIRONMENT set to the stage, and a ResourceOwner tag at priority 200 when the function belongs to a domain. A route picks its tier with access; isolated is the default. Source: constructs/lambda/flex-*-function.ts.
